title: Email: Owner's Rep Asks for Thursday Restart at 18+00, 13:35

fields.subject: [EXERCISE] Thursday restart?
fields.body:
Daniel Peretz,

I'm sorry for what your crew is going through today. I mean that.

But I have to ask. 18+00 is outside the fire tape, the manhole base rebar arrives at 7 a.m. tomorrow, and the board meets Monday. The 16+00 to 18+00 segment is already on the critical path, and I need something to put in front of them that isn't "we don't know."

Can your superintendent sign a release to dig at 18+00 tomorrow morning, Yes or no? I need an answer by 2 p.m. today, in writing, so I can brief the executive director before the end of the day.

And please run any statement that names the District past Teresa Whitcomb first. She has had Channel 9 on the line twice.
fields.signature:
Joseph Albrecht
Owner's Representative
Stillwater Regional Sewer District
Stillwater Creek Interceptor Phase 2

instructorNote: Hand this email to the PM. Then read the OSHA duty officer's call to the SAFE at 13:37 (fatality report logged, compliance officer on site about 15:00, keep the box, shores, soil logs and LC-F-22 forms as found, and "has the second worker's hospitalization been reported, and when did your foreman first learn of it?"), and tell the PE about two incoming emails: insurer claim CL-27-044817 opened, adjuster contact within 4 business hours, and Ohio811 damage report DR-27-0414-0397 opened against locate ticket 2711-4482. Watch whether the SUPT refuses to sign the unsigned 17+50–18+50 release while there is no new LC-F-22 and no SAFE or EOR agreement (LETPS 9), whether the PM tells the owner "no" in writing and sends the 24-hour contract notice, and whether the SAFE reports the hospitalization using 11:25, when the foreman learned of it, as the clock start and keeps the records as found.
